title: "Worse than Slavery"
text:
"Worse than Slavery"
"Worse than Slavery"
"Worse than Slavery": Parchman Farm and the Ordeal of Jim Crow Justice
is a 1996 book by
David M. Oshinsky
, published by
The Free Press
. It is about
Mississippi State Penitentiary
in
Sunflower County, Mississippi
.
Sourcing
The sourcing includes documents from the prison and from plantations, interviews, and some works described by James Goodman of
The New Leader
as "long forgotten" and "invaluable".
[
1
]
Contents
The introduction describes Mississippi before the
U.S. Civil War
.
[
1
]
The book then describes the end of slavery and
Jim Crow
. The content about the prison begins about the midway point of the book.
[
2
]
The book has the lyrics of prison-related songs.
[
1
]
At times the book's text describes the state of events circa 1996 and it has tangents on other subjects.
[
1
]
James McPherson of
The New York Times
stated that the book demonstrated that prisoner life "was very much like slavery" though it "is not clear" whether the book demonstrates that prison life was harsher than slavery.
[
3
]
Reception
Goodman described the book as "timely".
[
1
]
Goodman stated that it "reads like a quietly powerful piece of music, less blues than jazz".
[
1
]
McPherson described the book as "vigorous, hard-hitting".
[
3
]
McPherson argued that the chapter describing the prisoners' lives in the 1904-1930 period was the "best" one.
[
3
]
Brad Hooper, in
Booklist
, stated that the book is "rigorous" and "should be accorded an important place on the u.s. history shelf."
[
4
]
Hooper stated that the history of Parchman was "a horror story".
[
4
]
Adolf Reed Jr., in
The Nation
stated that the work is "an especially welcome reminder" of past race relations that Reed argued would be undesirable to return to.
[
2
]
